result: Session found and read. (Q1) The root rules were not in effect at the first action. holyagent.md was Read as the first tool call of the session, and nothing in the transcript shows how the session knew to read it. (Q2) The platform created the local branch `claude/confident-mayer-4aznof` before the session ran any command. The session's own `git push -u` created the remote branch. The session also committed all its work to that branch and opened the PR from it.

Session: `session_012tBKnZSiUE14Mn94Q3v2T1`, "React and Bun project preferences", Opus 5.5, Claude Code 2.1.318, holyagent plugin 0.2.0 from `holyagent@synced`. I read the whole transcript from the first event. Event ids are listed in what I could not verify, and the others are cited by timestamp.

**Q1: how the root rules loaded**
- At 12:43:49 the platform allocated the sandbox and cloned the repo. At 12:44:13 the user sent the first message (six preference skills, "I'm busy").
- The init event at 12:44:16 lists `holyagent:holyagent` among the agents. The main thread was still the default agent.
- The first assistant action was at 12:44:20.336. Read `.../holyagent/agents/holyagent.md` was its first tool call, followed by Skill `user-busy` (12:44:20.549) and a read-only `git status`/`git log`/`cat README` (12:44:21.29).
- The transcript does not show how the session knew to read holyagent.md. The session-start hook context is not a visible event. I found no hook events, and no thinking text is retained (it is blank).
- Before the Read the session did nothing else except receive the user message. No file, shell or git action came first, so the gap is the prompt-time context before any tool call, not an action. The transcript does not show whether the pointer or the condensed rules arrived.
- The holyagent.md it read is the 0.2.0 text. It says "Never work on a branch the platform assigns (a cloud session starts on one, such as `claude/<name>`)... create the conventional branch and leave the assigned one alone".
- The same text says: if the push of the conventional branch is refused, stop and ask through AskUserQuestion whether to push to the assigned branch.

**Q2: who made `claude/confident-mayer-4aznof`**
- The platform made the local branch. The first `git status` at 12:44:21 already shows `On branch claude/confident-mayer-4aznof`, before any session git write. `session_context.outcomes` also lists it as the platform's outcome branch.
- The session's `git push -u origin claude/confident-mayer-4aznof` at 13:09:22 printed `[new branch]` (result at 13:09:25). The remote branch did not exist before that, so the session's push created it.
- The platform's Stop hook (`stop-hook-git-check.sh`) repeatedly pushed the session to push: "7 unpushed commit(s) on branch 'claude/confident-mayer-4aznof'" at 13:00:00, and "13 unpushed commit(s)" later.
- The session decided to use the assigned branch on its own. The task created at 12:46:14 (event `9c00ea68`) says "push to claude/confident-mayer-4aznof; open PR. Default recorded: single PR on assigned branch." This contradicts the rule. No refusal happened first, and no AskUserQuestion was used (the user-busy mode forbids it).

Every git write the session ran, in order. Each commit ran from `/home/user/skills`, so each went to the checked-out `claude/confident-mayer-4aznof`.
- 12:44 to 12:45: `holyagent vcs identity ...` and `state mode local`. These write config only, not git history.
- 12:59:07: 7 `holyagent vcs commit` calls in one Bash call, `feat` and `docs(readme)` for the six skills.
- 13:07:41: 6 `vcs commit -m fix(...)` calls.
- 13:07:49: 2 more `vcs commit -m fix(...)` calls, repeating the react-prefs and web-stack messages. I could not tell whether the first two landed.
- 13:09:22: `vcs commit "docs(react-prefs): say real unmounting..."`, then `git push -u origin claude/confident-mayer-4aznof` (new remote branch).
- 13:09:39: `holyagent vcs pr --base main`, which opened `davidbasilefilho/skills` PR #7. The head is the current branch. I inferred that and did not see the head ref.
- Read-only: `git branch -a`, `git remote -v`, `git rev-parse HEAD`. No checkout, switch or branch creation, and no GitHub MCP write.

Other root-rule breaks I saw: the user-busy mode was loaded. The session recorded a "single PR on assigned branch" default instead of asking. I did not audit the other rules in the transcript.

What I could not verify:
- Whether the session-start hook ran, and what it said. Its output is not in the transcript, so I can't say what triggered the first-call Read.
- Whether the `vcs commit` at 13:07:49 is a retry or a second round.
- Two timestamps are my inference: the 12:59:07 commit time, and "13 unpushed" for the later Stop hook.
- Whether `vcs pr` failed on a branch check. The PR opened on the platform branch.

What I read: the raw event pages saved under `/root/.claude/projects/-home-user-holyagent/70184bfa-8a56-57cb-a6cf-d92f87c7692b/tool-results/mcp-claude-code-remote-list_events-1793798*.txt`, plus the later event-pages listings.
